answer.justification: The recurrent laryngeal nerve lies near the inferior thyroid artery and posterior thyroid lobe, so ligation close to the inferior pole during thyroidectomy risks nerve injury. This causes vocal cord paralysis and hoarseness. External laryngeal nerve injury relates to the superior thyroid artery, internal laryngeal nerve injury causes aspiration, and laryngeal edema would occur acutely.
